question.problem:
After applying the first coat of paint, the painter had $0.18$ liters of mixture left over. How much mixture did the painter use when applying the first coat of paint? Express your answer as a decimal.

The painter used$\,$
{{field-1}}
$\,$liters of the mixture when applying the first coat.
question.worked_solution:
In part 3, we found that the painter prepared $0.64$ liters of the mixture.

To determine the amount of mixture the painter used, we need to calculate $0.64-0.18.$

First, we line up the decimal points:

$$
\begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,-\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\, \\  &  &  & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, &  & \end{aligned}
$$

Next, we proceed by subtracting the two numbers just as we would with whole numbers:

$$
\begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,\,\begin{aligned} \\ \end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,\,\begin{aligned} \\ 5\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, & \begin{aligned}14\end{aligned} \\  &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,-\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\, \\  &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the painter used $0.46$ liters of the mixture when applying the first coat.

shared_context.problem: A workshop where cars are painted has ${(\frac{20}{9})}^{2}$ liters of paint available to paint some parts of a customer's car.

earlier_parts.problem:
Expressed as an improper fraction, the exact amount of paint available is$\,$

                            
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        
$\,$liters.

feedback.worked_solution:
The exact amount of paint is ${(\frac{20}{9})}^{2}$ liters.

Writing ${(\frac{20}{9})}^{2}$ with multiplication signs, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{20}{9})}^{2} & ={{\frac{20}{9}\times \frac{20}{9}}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ times}} \\  & =\frac{20\times 20}{9\times 9} \\  & =\frac{400}{81}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{(\frac{20}{9})}^{2}=\frac{400}{81}.
$$

earlier_parts.problem:
The instructions state that $0.6$ liters of thinner should be used for every liter of paint. How much thinner is needed if the painter plans to use $0.4$ liters of paint? Express your answer as a decimal.

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        The painter should use$\,$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        
$\,$liters of thinner with $0.4$ liters of paint.

feedback.worked_solution:
To determine the amount of thinner the painter should use with $0.4$ liters of paint, we have to multiply $0.6$ by $0.4.$

We proceed by multiplying the two numbers just as we would with whole numbers.

Notice that the second number has a leading $0$, which we ignore during the multiplication:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,\,\begin{aligned} \\ 2\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  \\  &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,.6\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,\times \,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,.4\,\,\,\, \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We now count the total number of decimal places in the two factors.

There is $1$ decimal place in $0.6$ and there is $1$ decimal place in $0.4.$
Therefore, their product will have $1+1=2$ decimal places.

So, we take our value of $24$ and add a decimal point to make a number with $2$ decimal places.

$$
\,\overset{↓}{.}\,\,\,{{24}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ digits}}
$$

Hence, $0.6\times 0.4=0.24.$

We conclude that the painter should use $0.24$ liters of thinner in $0.4$ liters of paint.

earlier_parts.problem:
To apply the first coat of paint, the painter mixes $0.4$ liters of paint with $0.24$ liters of thinner. What is the volume of the combined mixture?

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        Expressed as a decimal, the volume of the mixture equals$\,$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        
$\,$liters.

feedback.worked_solution:
To determine the volume of the mixture, we need to calculate the sum $0.4+0.24.$

There is $1$ decimal place in $0.4$ and $2$ decimal places in $0.24.$

To add the numbers, they both need to have the same number of decimals. Hence, we rewrite the first number so that it has $2$ decimal places:

$$
0.4=0.40
$$

Next, we line up the decimal points:

$$
\begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, \\  &  &  & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, &  & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we proceed by adding the two numbers just as we would with whole numbers:

$$
\begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,\begin{aligned} \\ \end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  &  \\  &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, \\  &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the mixture equals $0.64$ liters.
